meta.title: Who really said "The oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Goodreads credits Karl Marx. The sentence is Lenin's, from The State and Revolution (1917) — his own summary of Marx on the Paris Commune.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'The oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament'?
meta.ogDescription: Not Marx. Lenin wrote it in The State and Revolution, ch. 5 — paraphrasing Marx's Civil War in France. Sources fetched and checked.

answer.label: Not Karl Marx — actually Lenin, paraphrasing Marx
answer.sourceLine: This exact sentence is Lenin’s, from The State and Revolution (written August–September 1917, first published 1918), chapter 5, section 2 ↗: “Marx grasped this essence of capitalist democracy splendidly when, in analyzing the experience of the Commune, he said that the oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament!” Lenin is summarising Marx in his own words — note the indirect “he said that”, with no quotation marks — so the sentence circulating under Marx’s name is Lenin’s prose about Marx, not Marx’s prose. Marx’s own line, in The Civil War in France ↗, runs differently: “Instead of deciding once in three or six years which member of the ruling class was to misrepresent the people in Parliament…”

source.excerpt: Democracy for an insignificant minority, democracy for the rich — that is the democracy of capitalist society. … Marx grasped this essence of capitalist democracy splendidly when, in analyzing the experience of the Commune, he said that the oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament!
trail: Lenin’s The State and Revolution, ch. 5 ↗ contains the sentence verbatim, inside a paragraph about “democracy for the rich.”

Marx’s The Civil War in France ↗ — the Third Address of May 1871; the “ch05” in that URL is the archive’s file numbering, not a division of the work — does not contain it; his own formulation is “Instead of deciding once in three or six years which member of the ruling class was to misrepresent the people in Parliament…”
Wikiquote’s Lenin page ↗ lists it as sourced to The State and Revolution, ch. 5, while Wikiquote’s Karl Marx page ↗ files the same sentence under “Misattributed.”
The Marxists Internet Archive’s title page for the work ↗ gives “Written: August – September, 1917”, “First Published: 1918” and “Source: Collected Works, Volume 25.”
source.excerptNote: The giveaway is the grammar. Lenin writes “he said that the oppressed are allowed…” — reported speech, no quotation marks. Quote sites stripped the frame, kept the clause, and handed the words to the man being summarised.

sourceLink.text: The State and Revolution, chapter 5 (Marxists Internet Archive)

source.rightsNote: Lenin’s Russian original of 1918 is long out of copyright, but this exact English sentence belongs to a translation, and rights follow the translation. The Marxists Internet Archive credits its text to Lenin’s English Collected Works, vol. 25, and Open Library catalogues that volume ↗ as Progress Publishing, 1964 — well after the 1931 US public-domain line — so we treat the wording as in copyright. We found no pre-1931 English edition carrying this phrasing.

author.name: Vladimir Lenin
author.heading: About Vladimir Lenin
author.metaLine: 1870–1924 · Russian revolutionary, political theorist and first head of the Soviet government
author.bio: Vladimir Ilyich Lenin (born 22 April 1870, died 21 January 1924) was a Russian revolutionary, politician and political theorist, and the founding head of government of Soviet Russia and then the Soviet Union. He wrote The State and Revolution while in hiding in the late summer of 1917, weeks before the Bolsheviks took power — a book built almost entirely out of close readings of Marx and Engels. That method is why so many of its sharpest sentences, this one included, get handed back to the authors he was reading.

copyAttribution: "The oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament!" — V. I. Lenin, The State and Revolution (written 1917, first published 1918), ch. 5, sec. 2. Commonly misattributed to Karl Marx: Lenin was summarising Marx's argument in The Civil War in France (1871), where Marx's own wording is "Instead of deciding once in three or six years which member of the ruling class was to misrepresent the people in Parliament…"

misattribution.heading: How Lenin’s sentence became a Marx quote
misattribution.intro: Nobody invented this line out of thin air — the misattribution is baked into the sentence itself. Lenin wrote it about Marx, in reported speech, and the aggregators kept the clause and dropped the reporter.

items.why: Wikiquote’s Karl Marx page ↗ places the identical sentence in its Misattributed section, with the note that it is “Actually from State and Revolution by Vladimir Lenin, paraphrasing Marx in The Civil War in France.” The full wording, with “shall” and the closing “in parliament”, is Lenin’s throughout.

The Quotations Page ↗ prints “…which particular representatives of the oppressing class are to represent and repress them” — are to rather than shall, and no closing “in parliament” — credited to “Karl Marx, German economist & Communist political philosopher (1818 - 1883).” Goodreads ↗ carries this same truncated form under Marx’s name, liked more than 1,500 times.

items.scope: The argument, as opposed to the wording
items.why: The thought really is Marx’s, which is why the misattribution has survived. In The Civil War in France ↗ Marx wrote: “Instead of deciding once in three or six years which member of the ruling class was to misrepresent the people in Parliament, universal suffrage was to serve the people, constituted in Communes…” Same target, different sentence.

misattribution.truthLine: The words are Lenin’s, from The State and Revolution, ch. 5 ↗; the argument is Marx’s, from The Civil War in France ↗. Crediting Marx with the sentence is following Lenin’s own framing one step too far.

context.heading: Why Lenin was writing this
lead: Lenin wrote The State and Revolution in August and September 1917, in hiding from the Provisional Government, according to the Marxists Internet Archive’s notes on the work ↗; Wikipedia records that he had begun gathering material earlier, in Switzerland, under the working title “Marxism on the State.” The book is largely an exercise in reading Marx and Engels closely and drawing conclusions from them — which is exactly the mode this sentence is written in.

Chapter 5 argues that a capitalist republic offers “democracy for the rich”: a suffrage hedged by residence rules, exclusions and practical obstacles that squeeze the poor out of politics. The famous sentence is the punchline of that argument, and Lenin credits it to Marx’s dissection of the Paris Commune rather than claiming it himself. That generosity is the whole reason it now circulates with the wrong name on it.
detailsBody: There are two different English renderings of Marx’s underlying line, which adds to the confusion. The Marxists Internet Archive’s text of The Civil War in France has “which member of the ruling class was to misrepresent the people in Parliament,” while chapter 3 of The State and Revolution ↗ quotes Marx as “which member of the ruling class was to represent and repress [ver- and zertreten] the people in parliament.” Neither is the sentence people quote.

The Civil War in France was itself written in English by Marx and first published in 1871 as an address of the General Council of the International Working Men’s Association, so that text — unlike the Lenin translation quoted here — is in the public domain.
context.pull: Lenin wrote the sentence and handed the credit to Marx. The internet took him at his word.

sourcesVerified.claim: Lenin's The State and Revolution, ch. 5 §2, contains verbatim: "Marx grasped this essence of capitalist democracy splendidly when, in analyzing the experience of the Commune, he said that the oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament!" — reported speech, no quotation marks. The preceding paragraph begins "Democracy for an insignificant minority, democracy for the rich…"

Marx's The Civil War in France does NOT contain "oppressed are allowed once every few years" or "particular representatives of the oppressing class"; his wording is "Instead of deciding once in three or six years which member of the ruling class was to misrepresent the people in Parliament, universal suffrage was to serve the people, constituted in Communes…"

Ch. 3 of The State and Revolution (section "Abolition of Parliamentarism") quotes Marx as "Instead of deciding once in three or six years which member of the ruling class was to represent and repress [ver- and zertreten] the people in parliament…" — presented as a quotation from Marx, and not the popular sentence.

The Marxists Internet Archive title page for The State and Revolution states: Written: August - September, 1917; First Published: 1918; Source: Collected Works, Volume 25, p. 381-492. It also notes Lenin wrote it while in hiding from the Provisional Government.

Wikiquote's Vladimir Lenin page lists "The oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class shall represent and repress them in parliament!" as a sourced quote under the section for The State and Revolution (1917), cited to Ch. 5.

Wikiquote's Karl Marx page lists the same sentence under its "Misattributed" section with the note "Actually from State and Revolution by Vladimir Lenin, paraphrasing Marx in The Civil War in France." The page separately lists, under 1870s, Marx's genuine line sourced to The Civil War in France: "The Third Address" (May 1871).
Goodreads attributes the quote (in the shortened form "…are to represent and repress them.") to Karl Marx, with 1,535 likes.

The Quotations Page attributes "The oppressed are allowed once every few years to decide which particular representatives of the oppressing class are to represent and repress them." to "Karl Marx, German economist & Communist political philosopher (1818 - 1883)".
Open Library's catalogue record gives "Lenin Collected Works Volume 25 (June- September 1917)", publisher Progress Publishing, first published 1964.

Wikipedia states The State and Revolution was published in 1918 in Russian (Государство и революция), that Lenin began drafting in Switzerland in 1916 under the working title "Marxism on the State", and gives Lenin's dates as born 22 April 1870, died 21 January 1924, describing him as a Russian revolutionary, politician and political theorist and founding head of government of Soviet Russia and the Soviet Union.
